units.sourceHTML: 3.3 The s Command

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ command (as in substitute) is probably the most important in ⟦1⟧ and has a lot of different options. The syntax of the ⟦2⟧ command is ‘⟦3⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: The s command (as in substitute) is probably the most important in sed and has a lot of different options. The syntax of the s command is ‘s/regexp/replacement/flags’.

units.text: Its basic concept is simple: the ⟦0⟧ command attempts to match the pattern space against the supplied regular expression ⟦1⟧; if the match is successful, then that portion of the pattern space which was matched is replaced with ⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Its basic concept is simple: the s command attempts to match the pattern space against the supplied regular expression regexp; if the match is successful, then that portion of the pattern space which was matched is replaced with replacement.

units.text: For details about ⟦0⟧ syntax see ⟦1⟧Regular Expression Addresses⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: For details about regexp syntax see Regular Expression Addresses.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ can contain ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧ being a number from 1 to 9, inclusive) references, which refer to the portion of the match which is contained between the ⟦3⟧th ⟦4⟧ and its matching ⟦5⟧. Also, the ⟦6⟧ can contain unescaped ⟦7⟧ characters which reference the whole matched portion of the pattern space.
units.sourceHTML: The replacement can contain \n (n being a number from 1 to 9, inclusive) references, which refer to the portion of the match which is contained between the nth \( and its matching \). Also, the replacement can contain unescaped & characters which reference the whole matched portion of the pattern space.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ characters may be uniformly replaced by any other single character within any given ⟦1⟧ command. The ⟦2⟧ character (or whatever other character is used in its stead) can appear in the ⟦3⟧ or ⟦4⟧ only if it is preceded by a ⟦5⟧ character.
units.sourceHTML: The / characters may be uniformly replaced by any other single character within any given s command. The / character (or whatever other character is used in its stead) can appear in the regexp or replacement only if it is preceded by a \ character.

units.text: interaction in ⟦0⟧ command ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ Note: the ⟦3⟧POSIX⟦4⟧ standard does not specify what should happen when you mix the ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ modifiers, and currently there is no widely agreed upon meaning across ⟦7⟧ implementations. For GNU ⟦8⟧, the interaction is defined to be: ignore matches before the ⟦9⟧th, and then match and replace all matches from the ⟦10⟧th on.

For GNU sed, the interaction is defined to be: ignore matches before the numberth, and then match and replace all matches from the numberth on.

units.text: If the substitution was made, then print the new pattern space.
units.sourceHTML: If the substitution was made, then print the new pattern space.

units.text: Note: when both the ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ options are specified, the relative ordering of the two produces very different results. In general, ⟦2⟧ (evaluate then print) is what you want, but operating the other way round can be useful for debugging. For this reason, the current version of GNU ⟦3⟧ interprets specially the presence of ⟦4⟧ options both before and after ⟦5⟧, printing the pattern space before and after evaluation, while in general flags for the ⟦6⟧ command show their effect just once. This behavior, although documented, might change in future versions.
units.sourceHTML: Note: when both the p and e options are specified, the relative ordering of the two produces very different results. In general, ep (evaluate then print) is what you want, but operating the other way round can be useful for debugging. For this reason, the current version of GNU sed interprets specially the presence of p options both before and after e, printing the pattern space before and after evaluation, while in general flags for the s command show their effect just once. This behavior, although documented, might change in future versions.

units.text: This command allows one to pipe input from a shell command into pattern space. If a substitution was made, the command that is found in pattern space is executed and pattern space is replaced with its output. A trailing newline is suppressed; results are undefined if the command to be executed contains a ⟦0⟧NUL⟦1⟧ character. This is a GNU ⟦2⟧ extension.
units.sourceHTML: This command allows one to pipe input from a shell command into pattern space. If a substitution was made, the command that is found in pattern space is executed and pattern space is replaced with its output. A trailing newline is suppressed; results are undefined if the command to be executed contains a NUL character. This is a GNU sed extension.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ modifier to regular-expression matching is a GNU extension which makes ⟦1⟧ match ⟦2⟧ in a case-insensitive manner.
units.sourceHTML: The I modifier to regular-expression matching is a GNU extension which makes sed match regexp in a case-insensitive manner.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ modifier to regular-expression matching is a GNU ⟦1⟧ extension which directs GNU ⟦2⟧ to match the regular expression in ⟦3⟧multi-line⟦4⟧ mode. The modifier causes ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ to match respectively (in addition to the normal behavior) the empty string after a newline, and the empty string before a newline. There are special character sequences (⟦7⟧ and ⟦8⟧) which always match the beginning or the end of the buffer. In addition, the period character does not match a new-line character in multi-line mode.
units.sourceHTML: The M modifier to regular-expression matching is a GNU sed extension which directs GNU sed to match the regular expression in multi-line mode. The modifier causes ^ and $ to match respectively (in addition to the normal behavior) the empty string after a newline, and the empty string before a newline. There are special character sequences (\` and \') which always match the beginning or the end of the buffer. In addition, the period character does not match a new-line character in multi-line mode.
